top_choice_rationale: Mircea Cărtărescu (P001) is the only writer on the slate, and I judge him by the common criteria rather than by the shared opening first places. The voice is distinctive in long, patterned sentences and recurring imagery of body, memory and cosmology. As publicly known, Blinding and Solenoid show formal control at very large scale, and the imaginative depth is built into the architecture of the books. The oeuvre is long enough to judge as a whole, and my round-2 citation names prose as the core with poetry as its ground. Caveats: I rely on translation and reception, not on the Romanian originals. I cannot verify whether the later very long novels deepen the early project or only extend it, and coverage of the poetry and essays in translation is thinner than for the novels. The question of how the will's idealistic tendency applies to an inward and often disturbing project remains one of interpretation. These reservations do not outweigh the case for the award, so no-award (P000) ranks below.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my writing on Central Europe concerns a region adjacent to Romania, which is context only and not a connection to the candidate
